environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed in account 987654321098 under OU 'ou-prod-workloads'. The execution role 'webhook-processor-role-prod' has an attached permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::987654321098:policy/LambdaWorkloadCeiling) that uses an explicit Deny with StringNotEquals condition on aws:RequestedRegion and denies iam:Create*, iam:Attach*, iam:Put*, iam:Delete*, sts:AssumeRole (except self), and lambda:UpdateFunctionCode. Additionally, the organizational SCP 'scp-restrict-credential-usage' attached at the OU level contains a Deny statement for iam:CreateUser, iam:CreateAccessKey, iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy with a condition that aws:PrincipalOrgID matches and the principal ARN contains ':role/webhook-'. The SCP uses a NotAction/Deny pattern where the allowed actions are explicitly scoped to dynamodb:PutItem, dynamodb:GetItem, logs:*, and xray:*. The Lambda VPC security group egress rules permit TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 but the NACL on the Lambda subnet blocks outbound TCP 80 to 169.254.169.254/32 (rule 50, deny) before the allow-all rule (rule 100). Note: the DNS rebinding itself may still resolve to 169.254.169.254 but the HTTP fetch on port 80 to that IP is network-blocked, and even if credentials were somehow obtained, both the permission boundary and SCP independently deny the IAM escalation actions.
